results.content:

## What Tesla Actually Announced on November 21

Tesla said V15 is starting to roll out and that it upgrades every part of the end-to-end driving network. That sentence matters more than it first appears. An end-to-end system takes camera input and produces driving output through a learned model, rather than passing hand-written rules between separate modules. Saying every part of that network changed suggests a broad retrain, not a patch to one feature. [...] Neither design has a proven win on these specific hazards in the public record we reviewed. The deployment contexts also differ, since Tesla’s system is supervised on customer cars while some rivals run driverless in limited areas. Comparing a supervised feature with a driverless service on detection alone would mislead readers.

## Historical Context: From V14 to V15

V15 follows V14, which our coverage tracked through owner tests and safety debates. The jump in major version number invites expectation of a large change, and Tesla’s wording about upgrading every part of the end-to-end network fits that framing. Version numbers at Tesla do not follow a public specification, though, so a new major number proves little by itself. [...] Beyond hazard detection, Tesla lists more natural speed handling in school zones and inclement weather. Both are places where a driver-assistance system tends to feel wrong even when it is technically legal. Too slow in a school zone annoys followers. Too fast in rain frightens the driver.

Natural is a subjective word, and Tesla has not attached numbers to it. We do not know target speeds, how the system detects a school zone, or whether it relies on signs, map data or both. Road signs sit on the detection list, so sign reading may play a part, but that is an inference and not something Tesla stated.

results.title: Tesla launches FSD v15, targets its biggest weaknesses, from signs to potholes | Electrek
results.content:
The driving side is harder to judge. Tesla is going straight at the weaknesses that owners and regulators complain about most: misread speed limits, potholes, school zones, debris. If v15 delivers real progress on all of those, it’s a really good update.

But “improved detection” doesn’t tell us how much better, and a 25x multiplier without the underlying number is hard to check. FSD has gone two steps forward, one step back throughout its history, with point releases regularly breaking things the previous version handled fine. And Tesla still won’t publish the disengagement data that would settle it. [...] > v15 upgrades every part of the end-to-end driving network. Includes:
> 
> Upgraded vision encoder shared between FSD, Robotaxi, and Optimus, which is trained on millions of internet videos for improved generalization and data efficiency, improving the critical intervention rate by 25x.
> 
> Introduced Tesla Augmented Reality, replacing all of the explicit model signals into a single end-to-end visualization using less total compute.
> 
> Improved navigation by using an end-to-end learned model based on route preference data from the fleet.
> 
> Improved parking location selection by using personalized parking history, and the map will now display multiple parking options at your destination.
> [...] Tesla calls it “Reality View” in its announcement and “Tesla Augmented Reality” in the release notes. The notes say it replaces all the separate model signals with a single end-to-end visualization that uses less compute, and Tesla says it lets the driver “see & control what FSD is planning to do.” If that works as advertised, it could make supervising the system a lot easier.

## v15 goes after FSD’s biggest weak spots

What stands out more is where Tesla is focusing. Almost every driving improvement in the release notes targets an area where FSD struggles today.

results.title: Tesla Full Self-Driving v15: a first-hand look at Reality View, new features
results.content:
FSD still struggles with parking, it has routine bugs from update to update, it does not recognize potholes or large bumps on the road, speed control is a common complaint, and Navigation has been one of the biggest pain points.

However, v15 will likely bring massive improvements to capability and give people more options, like potentially parking orientation and more refined spot selection. We can only wait and see what Tesla will include.

results.title: Tesla FSD V15 Offers Stunning Visualizations That Distract From “25x”
results.content:
The visualization is cool, and a real achievement, but it does not affect the driving performance of the system, and in fact you should not have something distracting on the screen when your eyes are supposed to be on the road. Far more interesting is the second line in their release notes:

> v15 upgrades every part of the end-to-end driving network. Includes:

> - Upgraded vision encoder shared between FSD, Robotaxi, and Optimus, which is trained on millions of internet videos for improved generalization and data efficiency, improving the critical intervention rate by 25x.

> - Introduced Tesla Reality View, replacing all of the explicit model signals into a single end-to-end visualization using less total compute.
